and fulfils (5.2)–(5.6) in variational form, i.e. it satisfies

⟨ξt,w⟩V+(∇η,∇w)H=(P′​(φ¯)​(σ¯−μ¯)​ξ+P⁡(φ¯)​(ρ−η)−𝕙′​(φ¯)​u¯​ξ−𝕙⁡(φ¯)​h,w)H,\displaystyle\langle\xi_{t},w\rangle_{V}+(\nabla\eta,\nabla w)_{H}=(P^{\prime}(\overline{\varphi})(\overline{\sigma}-\overline{\mu})\xi+P(\overline{\varphi})(\rho-\eta)-\mathbbm{h}^{\prime}(\overline{\varphi})\overline{u}\,\xi-\mathbbm{h}(\overline{\varphi})h,w)_{H},
(η,w)H=(A​F′​(φ¯)​ξ+B​a​ξ−B​J∗ξ,w)H,\displaystyle(\eta,w)_{H}=(AF^{\prime}(\overline{\varphi})\xi+Ba\xi-BJ\ast\xi,w)_{H},
⟨ρt,w⟩V+(∇ρ,∇w)H=−(P′​(φ¯)​(σ¯−μ¯)​ξ+P⁡(φ¯)​(ρ−η),w)H+(k,w)H,\displaystyle\langle\rho_{t},w\rangle_{V}+(\nabla\rho,\nabla w)_{H}=-(P^{\prime}(\overline{\varphi})(\overline{\sigma}-\overline{\mu})\xi+P(\overline{\varphi})(\rho-\eta),w)_{H}+(k,w)_{H},

for a.e. t∈(0,T)t\in(0,T) and for any w∈Vw\in V, and ξ⁡(0)=0\xi(0)=0, ρ⁡(0)=0\rho(0)=0.

Proof.

We proceed formally, but we recall that the argument can be made rigorous by employing a Faedo-Galerkin discretisation scheme, with discrete spaces made of eigenvectors of the operator 𝒩\mathcal{N}. Then, being the system linear, it is a standard matter to pass to the limit in the discretisation framework and recover a weak solution with the expected regularities. For the main estimate, we test equation (5.2) by ξ\xi, (5.4) by ρ\rho and sum them up, to obtain:

12​dd​t​∥ξ∥H2+12​dd​t​∥ρ∥H2+(∇η,∇ξ)H+∥∇ρ∥H2\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\lVert\xi\rVert^{2}_{H}+\frac{1}{2}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\lVert\rho\rVert^{2}_{H}+(\nabla\eta,\nabla\xi)_{H}+\lVert\nabla\rho\rVert^{2}_{H}
≤(P′​(φ¯)​(σ¯−μ¯)​ξ,ξ−ρ)H+(P⁡(φ¯)​(ρ−η),ξ−ρ)H−(𝕙′​(φ¯)​u¯​ξ+𝕙⁡(φ¯)​h,ξ)H+(k,ρ)H.\displaystyle\hskip 10.00002pt\leq(P^{\prime}(\overline{\varphi})(\overline{\sigma}-\overline{\mu})\xi,\xi-\rho)_{H}+(P(\overline{\varphi})(\rho-\eta),\xi-\rho)_{H}-(\mathbbm{h}^{\prime}(\overline{\varphi})\overline{u}\,\xi+\mathbbm{h}(\overline{\varphi})h,\xi)_{H}+(k,\rho)_{H}.

Then, by using Remark 4.3, Cauchy-Schwarz and Young’s inequalities and by recalling that ∥σ¯−μ¯∥L∞​(Ω)∈L∞​(0,T)\lVert\overline{\sigma}-\overline{\mu}\rVert_{L^{\infty}(\Omega)}\in L^{\infty}(0,T) by Theorem 4.8, we estimate the right-hand side as

12​dd​t​∥ξ∥H2+12​dd​t​∥ρ∥H2+(∇η,∇ξ)H+∥∇ρ∥H2\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\lVert\xi\rVert^{2}_{H}+\frac{1}{2}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\lVert\rho\rVert^{2}_{H}+(\nabla\eta,\nabla\xi)_{H}+\lVert\nabla\rho\rVert^{2}_{H}
≤C⁡(1+∥σ¯−μ¯∥L∞​(Ω)2)​∥ξ∥H2+C​∥η∥H2+C​∥ρ∥H2+C​∥h∥H2+C​∥k∥H2.\displaystyle\hskip 10.00002pt\leq C\left(1+\lVert\overline{\sigma}-\overline{\mu}\rVert^{2}_{L^{\infty}(\Omega)}\right)\lVert\xi\rVert^{2}_{H}+C\lVert\eta\rVert^{2}_{H}+C\lVert\rho\rVert^{2}_{H}+C\lVert h\rVert^{2}_{H}+C\lVert k\rVert^{2}_{H}.

Next, to close the estimate, we further test (5.3) by −Δ​ξ-\Delta\xi, which is possible within the discretisation framework, and integrate by parts, by recalling that, due to the fact that the discrete spaces are made of functions satisfying homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions, no extra boundary terms appear. Then, by exploiting Hölder, Young and Gagliardo-Nirenberg (2.1) inequalities, together with Remark 4.3 and hypotheses A3 and A2, we infer that

(∇η,∇ξ)H\displaystyle(\nabla\eta,\nabla\xi)_{H} =(AF′′′(φ¯)∇φ¯ξ,∇ξ)H+((AF′′(φ¯)+Ba)∇ξ,∇ξ)H\displaystyle=(AF^{\prime\prime\prime}(\overline{\varphi})\nabla\overline{\varphi}\,\xi,\nabla\xi)_{H}+((AF^{\prime\prime}(\overline{\varphi})+Ba)\nabla\xi,\nabla\xi)_{H}
+(B∇aξ,∇ξ)H−(B∇J∗ξ,∇ξ)H\displaystyle\hskip 10.00002pt+(B\nabla a\,\xi,\nabla\xi)_{H}-(B\nabla J\ast\xi,\nabla\xi)_{H}
≥c0​∥∇ξ∥H2−C​∥∇φ¯∥L6​(Ω)​∥ξ∥L3​(Ω)​∥∇ξ∥H−2​B​b∗​∥ξ∥H​∥∇ξ∥H\displaystyle\geq c_{0}\lVert\nabla\xi\rVert^{2}_{H}-C\lVert\nabla\overline{\varphi}\rVert_{L^{6}(\Omega)}\lVert\xi\rVert_{L^{3}(\Omega)}\lVert\nabla\xi\rVert_{H}-2Bb^{\ast}\lVert\xi\rVert_{H}\lVert\nabla\xi\rVert_{H}
≥c0​∥∇ξ∥H2−C​∥∇φ¯∥L6​(Ω)​∥ξ∥H1/2​∥ξ∥V3/2−2​B​b∗​∥ξ∥H​∥∇ξ∥H\displaystyle\geq c_{0}\lVert\nabla\xi\rVert^{2}_{H}-C\lVert\nabla\overline{\varphi}\rVert_{L^{6}(\Omega)}\lVert\xi\rVert^{1/2}_{H}\lVert\xi\rVert^{3/2}_{V}-2Bb^{\ast}\lVert\xi\rVert_{H}\lVert\nabla\xi\rVert_{H}
≥c02​∥∇ξ∥H2+C⁡(1+∥∇φ¯∥L6​(Ω)4)​∥ξ∥H2,\displaystyle\geq\frac{c_{0}}{2}\lVert\nabla\xi\rVert^{2}_{H}+C\left(1+\lVert\nabla\overline{\varphi}\rVert^{4}_{L^{6}(\Omega)}\right)\lVert\xi\rVert^{2}_{H},

where ∥∇φ¯∥L6​(Ω)4∈L∞​(0,T)\lVert\nabla\overline{\varphi}\rVert^{4}_{L^{6}(\Omega)}\in L^{\infty}(0,T) by Theorem 4.8 and Sobolev embeddings. Therefore, by putting all together, we have the estimate:

12​dd​t​∥ξ∥H2+12​dd​t​∥ρ∥H2+c02​∥∇ξ∥H2+∥∇ρ∥H2\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\lVert\xi\rVert^{2}_{H}+\frac{1}{2}\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\lVert\rho\rVert^{2}_{H}+\frac{c_{0}}{2}\lVert\nabla\xi\rVert^{2}_{H}+\lVert\nabla\rho\rVert^{2}_{H}
≤C⁡(1+∥∇φ¯∥L6​(Ω)4+∥σ¯−μ¯∥L∞​(Ω)2)​∥ξ∥H2+C​∥η∥H2+C​∥ρ∥H2+C​∥h∥H2+C​∥k∥H2.\displaystyle\hskip 10.00002pt\leq C\left(1+\lVert\nabla\overline{\varphi}\rVert^{4}_{L^{6}(\Omega)}+\lVert\overline{\sigma}-\overline{\mu}\rVert^{2}_{L^{\infty}(\Omega)}\right)\lVert\xi\rVert^{2}_{H}+C\lVert\eta\rVert^{2}_{H}+C\lVert\rho\rVert^{2}_{H}+C\lVert h\rVert^{2}_{H}+C\lVert k\rVert^{2}_{H}.

Now observe that, by comparison in equation (5.3), thanks to Remark 4.3 and hypothesis A2, one can easily see that

∥η∥H2≤C​∥ξ∥H2.\lVert\eta\rVert^{2}_{H}\leq C\lVert\xi\rVert^{2}_{H}. (5.7)

Hence, by also integrating on (0,t)(0,t), for any t∈(0,T)t\in(0,T), from the previous inequality we deduce that

12​∥ξ⁡(t)∥H2+12​∥ρ⁡(t)∥H2+c02​∫0t∥∇ξ∥H2​𝑑s+∫0t∥∇ρ∥H2​𝑑s\displaystyle\frac{1}{2}\lVert\xi(t)\rVert^{2}_{H}+\frac{1}{2}\lVert\rho(t)\rVert^{2}_{H}+\frac{c_{0}}{2}\int_{0}^{t}\lVert\nabla\xi\rVert^{2}_{H}\,\mathrm{d}s+\int_{0}^{t}\lVert\nabla\rho\rVert^{2}_{H}\,\mathrm{d}s
≤C​∫0T(1+∥∇φ¯∥L6​(Ω)4+∥σ¯−μ¯∥L∞​(Ω)2)​∥ξ∥H2​𝑑s+C​∫0T∥ρ∥H2+∥h∥H2+∥k∥H2​𝑑s,\displaystyle\hskip 10.00002pt\leq C\int_{0}^{T}\left(1+\lVert\nabla\overline{\varphi}\rVert^{4}_{L^{6}(\Omega)}+\lVert\overline{\sigma}-\overline{\mu}\rVert^{2}_{L^{\infty}(\Omega)}\right)\lVert\xi\rVert^{2}_{H}\,\mathrm{d}s+C\int_{0}^{T}\lVert\rho\rVert^{2}_{H}+\lVert h\rVert^{2}_{H}+\lVert k\rVert^{2}_{H}\,\mathrm{d}s,

which, by Gronwall’s lemma, implies the following uniform estimate:

∥ξ∥L∞​(0,T,H)∩L2​(0,T,V)2+∥ρ∥L∞​(0,T,H)∩L2​(0,T,V)2≤C⁡(∥h∥L2​(0,T,H)2+∥k∥L2​(0,T,H)2),\lVert\xi\rVert^{2}_{L^{\infty}(0,T;H)\cap L^{2}(0,T;V)}+\lVert\rho\rVert^{2}_{L^{\infty}(0,T;H)\cap L^{2}(0,T;V)}\leq C\left(\lVert h\rVert^{2}_{L^{2}(0,T;H)}+\lVert k\rVert^{2}_{L^{2}(0,T;H)}\right), (5.8)

with C>0C>0 depending only on the parameters of the system. Next, by testing (5.3) by −Δ​η-\Delta\eta, integrating by parts and using Hölder and Young’s inequalities, we obtain that

∥∇η∥H2\displaystyle\lVert\nabla\eta\rVert^{2}_{H} =(AF′′′(φ¯)∇φ¯ξ,∇η)H+((AF′′(φ¯)+Ba)∇ξ,∇η)H\displaystyle=(AF^{\prime\prime\prime}(\overline{\varphi})\nabla\overline{\varphi}\,\xi,\nabla\eta)_{H}+((AF^{\prime\prime}(\overline{\varphi})+Ba)\nabla\xi,\nabla\eta)_{H}
+(B∇aξ,∇η)H−(B∇J∗ξ,∇η)H\displaystyle\hskip 10.00002pt+(B\nabla a\,\xi,\nabla\eta)_{H}-(B\nabla J\ast\xi,\nabla\eta)_{H}
≤12​∥∇η∥H2+C​∥∇φ¯∥L4​(Ω)2⏟∈L∞​(0,T)​∥ξ∥L4​(Ω)2+C​∥ξ∥V2≤12​∥∇η∥H2+C​∥ξ∥V2,\displaystyle\leq\frac{1}{2}\lVert\nabla\eta\rVert^{2}_{H}+C\underbrace{\lVert\nabla\overline{\varphi}\rVert^{2}_{L^{4}(\Omega)}}_{\in L^{\infty}(0,T)}\lVert\xi\rVert^{2}_{L^{4}(\Omega)}+C\lVert\xi\rVert^{2}_{V}\leq\frac{1}{2}\lVert\nabla\eta\rVert^{2}_{H}+C\lVert\xi\rVert^{2}_{V},

which, by integrating on (0,T)(0,T) and applying (5.8), together with (5.7), implies that

∥η∥L∞​(0,T,H)∩L2​(0,T,V)2≤C⁡(∥h∥L2​(0,T,H)2+∥k∥L2​(0,T,H)2).\lVert\eta\rVert^{2}_{L^{\infty}(0,T;H)\cap L^{2}(0,T;V)}\leq C\left(\lVert h\rVert^{2}_{L^{2}(0,T;H)}+\lVert k\rVert^{2}_{L^{2}(0,T;H)}\right).

Finally, by comparison in (5.2) and (5.4), it also follows that

∥ξ∥H1​(0,T,V∗)2+∥ρ∥H1​(0,T,V∗)2≤C⁡(∥h∥L2​(0,T,H)2+∥k∥L2​(0,T,H)2).\lVert\xi\rVert^{2}_{H^{1}(0,T;V^{*})}+\lVert\rho\rVert^{2}_{H^{1}(0,T;V^{*})}\leq C\left(\lVert h\rVert^{2}_{L^{2}(0,T;H)}+\lVert k\rVert^{2}_{L^{2}(0,T;H)}\right).

In the end, by also using standard embeddings of Lebesgue-Bochner spaces on a Hilbert triplet, we have shown that there exists a constant C>0C>0, depending only on the parameters of the system, such that

∥ξ∥H1​(0,T,V∗)∩𝒞0​([0,T],H)∩L2​(0,T,V)2+∥η∥L∞​(0,T,H)∩L2​(0,T,V)2+∥ρ∥H1​(0,T,V∗)∩𝒞0​([0,T],H)∩L2​(0,T,V)2≤C⁡(∥h∥L2​(0,T,H)2+∥k∥L2​(0,T,H)2).\begin{split}&\lVert\xi\rVert^{2}_{H^{1}(0,T;V^{*})\cap\mathcal{C}^{0}([0,T];H)\cap L^{2}(0,T;V)}+\lVert\eta\rVert^{2}_{L^{\infty}(0,T;H)\cap L^{2}(0,T;V)}\\ &\quad+\lVert\rho\rVert^{2}_{H^{1}(0,T;V^{*})\cap\mathcal{C}^{0}([0,T];H)\cap L^{2}(0,T;V)}\leq C\left(\lVert h\rVert^{2}_{L^{2}(0,T;H)}+\lVert k\rVert^{2}_{L^{2}(0,T;H)}\right).\end{split} (5.9)

With this estimate, it is a standard matter to pass to the limit in the discretisation and show the existence of a weak solution to (5.2)–(5.6). Moreover, due to the linearity of the system, this same estimate also gives uniqueness of the solution. This concludes the proof of Theorem 5.3. ∎

Remark 5.4.

We observe that the linearised system (5.2)–(5.6) is exactly the same as the abstract linearised system (3.7) with 𝛙=(φ¯,σ¯)⊤\boldsymbol{\uppsi}=(\overline{\varphi},\overline{\sigma})^{\top}, 𝛏=(ξ,ρ)⊤\boldsymbol{\upxi}=(\xi,\rho)^{\top}, 𝒇=(−𝕙⁡(φ¯)​h,k)⊤\boldsymbol{f}=(-\mathbbm{h}(\overline{\varphi})h,k)^{\top} and 𝒈=𝟎\boldsymbol{g}=\boldsymbol{0}. This means that, since (h,k)(h,k) can be taken in L∞​(QT)2L^{\infty}(Q_{T})^{2} and φ¯\overline{\varphi} can be embedded into 𝒞0​(QT¯)\mathcal{C}^{0}(\overline{Q_{T}}), one could follow the same argument used in the first part of the proof of Theorem 3.10, to say that there exists a unique maximal solution with regularity

ξ,ρ∈W1,p​(0,T,Lp​(Ω))∩Lp​(0,T,W2,p​(Ω)),for any p>N+2.\xi,\rho\in W^{1,p}(0,T;L^{p}(\Omega))\cap L^{p}(0,T;W^{2,p}(\Omega)),\hskip 10.00002pt\text{for any $p>N+2$.}

This can clearly be done in place of the previous proof, but the actual regularity that we need on the linearised system to study the optimal control problem is way less that the one guaranteed by maximal regularity theory. This is the reason we also provided the proof above.

5.2 Differentiability of the control-to-state operator

In order to study the control-to-state operator 𝒮\mathcal{S}, which associates to any control (u,v)∈𝒰ad×𝒱ad(u,v)\in\mathcal{U}_{\text{ad}}\times\mathcal{V}_{\text{ad}} the corresponding solution of the system (1.7)–(1.11), we introduce the following spaces:

𝕐\displaystyle\mathbb{Y} :=(H1​(0,T,H)∩L∞​(0,T,V)∩L2​(0,T,H2​(Ω)))3,\displaystyle:=(H^{1}(0,T;H)\cap L^{\infty}(0,T;V)\cap L^{2}(0,T;H^{2}(\Omega)))^{3},
𝕎\displaystyle\mathbb{W} :=(H1​(0,T,V∗)∩𝒞0​([0,T],H)∩L2​(0,T,V))×(L∞​(0,T,H)∩L2​(0,T,V))\displaystyle:=(H^{1}(0,T;V^{*})\cap\mathcal{C}^{0}([0,T];H)\cap L^{2}(0,T;V))\times(L^{\infty}(0,T;H)\cap L^{2}(0,T;V))
×(H1​(0,T,V∗)∩𝒞0​([0,T],H)∩L2​(0,T,V)).\displaystyle\hskip 20.00003pt\times(H^{1}(0,T;V^{*})\cap\mathcal{C}^{0}([0,T];H)\cap L^{2}(0,T;V)).

Observe that the space of strong solutions 𝕏\mathbb{X} is continuously embedded into 𝕐\mathbb{Y}, which is exactly the space where we proved the continuous dependence estimates. Indeed, from Theorem 4.8 and Theorem 4.11 we respectively know that

𝒮:L∞​(QT)2→𝕏is well-defined and\mathcal{S}:L^{\infty}(Q_{T})^{2}\to\mathbb{X}\hskip 10.00002pt\hbox{is well-defined and}
𝒮:L∞​(QT)2→𝕐is locally Lipschitz-continuous.\mathcal{S}:L^{\infty}(Q_{T})^{2}\to\mathbb{Y}\hskip 10.00002pt\hbox{is locally Lipschitz-continuous.}

Now, for R>0R>0, we fix an open set 𝒰R×𝒱R⊆L∞​(QT)2\mathcal{U}_{R}\times\mathcal{V}_{R}\subseteq L^{\infty}(Q_{T})^{2} such that 𝒰ad×𝒱ad⊆𝒰R×𝒱R\mathcal{U}_{\text{ad}}\times\mathcal{V}_{\text{ad}}\subseteq\mathcal{U}_{R}\times\mathcal{V}_{R}. Indeed, by hypothesis C3, we can take:

𝒰R:={u∈L∞​(QT)∣∥u∥L∞​(QT)<Mu+R},\displaystyle\mathcal{U}_{R}:=\{u\in L^{\infty}(Q_{T})\mid\lVert u\rVert_{L^{\infty}(Q_{T})}<M_{u}+R\}, 𝒱R:={v∈L∞​(QT)∣∥v∥L∞​(QT)<Mv+R},\displaystyle\mathcal{V}_{R}:=\{v\in L^{\infty}(Q_{T})\mid\lVert v\rVert_{L^{\infty}(Q_{T})}<M_{v}+R\},

where Mu=∥umax∥∞M_{u}=\lVert u_{\text{max}}\rVert_{\infty} and Mv=∥vmax∥∞M_{v}=\lVert v_{\text{max}}\rVert_{\infty}. Note that, in 𝒰R×𝒱R\mathcal{U}_{R}\times\mathcal{V}_{R}, the continuous dependence estimate of Theorem 4.11 holds with KK depending only on RR and the fixed data of the system. Our aim is to show that 𝒮:𝒰R×𝒱R→𝕎\mathcal{S}:\mathcal{U}_{R}\times\mathcal{V}_{R}\to\mathbb{W} is also Fréchet-differentiable in the larger space 𝕎\mathbb{W}. Indeed, we can prove the following theorem:

Theorem 5.5.

Assume hypothesis A1–A7, B1–B2 and C4–C5. Then 𝒮:𝒰R×𝒱R→𝕎\mathcal{S}:\mathcal{U}_{R}\times\mathcal{V}_{R}\to\mathbb{W} is Fréchet-differentiable, i.e. for any (u¯,v¯)∈𝒰R×𝒱R(\overline{u},\overline{v})\in\mathcal{U}_{R}\times\mathcal{V}_{R} there exists a unique Fréchet-derivative D​𝒮​(u¯,v¯)∈ℒ⁡(L∞​(QT)2,𝕎)D\mathcal{S}(\overline{u},\overline{v})\in\mathcal{L}(L^{\infty}(Q_{T})^{2},\mathbb{W}) such that:

∥𝒮⁡(u¯+h,v¯+k)−𝒮⁡(u¯,v¯)−D​𝒮​(u¯,v¯)​[h,k]∥𝕎∥(h,k)∥L2​(QT)2→0as ​∥(h,k)∥L2​(QT)2→0.\frac{\lVert\mathcal{S}(\overline{u}+h,\overline{v}+k)-\mathcal{S}(\overline{u},\overline{v})-D\mathcal{S}(\overline{u},\overline{v})[h,k]\rVert_{\mathbb{W}}}{\lVert(h,k)\rVert_{L^{2}(Q_{T})^{2}}}\to 0\hskip 10.00002pt\text{as }\lVert(h,k)\rVert_{L^{2}(Q_{T})^{2}}\to 0. (5.10)

Moreover, for any (h,k)∈L∞​(QT)2(h,k)\in L^{\infty}(Q_{T})^{2}, the Fréchet-derivative at (u¯,v¯)(\overline{u},\overline{v}) in (h,k)(h,k), which we denote by D​𝒮​(u¯,v¯)​[h,k]D\mathcal{S}(\overline{u},\overline{v})[h,k], is defined as the solution (ξ,η,ρ)(\xi,\eta,\rho) to the linearised system (5.2)–(5.6) corresponding to (φ¯,μ¯,σ¯)=𝒮⁡(u¯,v¯)(\overline{\varphi},\overline{\mu},\overline{\sigma})=\mathcal{S}(\overline{u},\overline{v}), with data hh and kk.

Remark 5.6.

Note that, by Theorem 5.3, D​𝒮​(u¯,v¯)D\mathcal{S}(\overline{u},\overline{v}) as defined above actually belongs to the space of continuous linear operators ℒ⁡(L∞​(QT)2,𝕎)\mathcal{L}(L^{\infty}(Q_{T})^{2},\mathbb{W}). Observe also that (5.10) shows Fréchet-differentiability with respect to the L2​(QT)L^{2}(Q_{T}) norm, but clearly, since L∞​(QT)↪L2​(QT)L^{\infty}(Q_{T})\hookrightarrow L^{2}(Q_{T}), this also implies Fréchet-differentiability in the correct space.

Proof.

We observe that it is sufficient to prove the result for any small enough perturbation (h,k)(h,k), i.e. we fix Λ>0\Lambda>0 and consider only perturbations such that

∥(h,k)∥L2​(QT)2≤Λ.\lVert(h,k)\rVert_{L^{2}(Q_{T})^{2}}\leq\Lambda. (5.11)

Now, we fix u¯\overline{u}, v¯\overline{v}, hh and kk as above and consider

(φ,μ,σ):=𝒮⁡(u¯+h,v¯+k),\displaystyle(\varphi,\mu,\sigma):=\mathcal{S}(\overline{u}+h,\overline{v}+k),
(φ¯,μ¯,σ¯):=𝒮⁡(u¯,v¯),\displaystyle(\overline{\varphi},\overline{\mu},\overline{\sigma}):=\mathcal{S}(\overline{u},\overline{v}),
(ξ,η,ρ)​ as the solution to (5.2)–(5.6) with respect to ​(h,k).\displaystyle(\xi,\eta,\rho)\text{ as the solution to \eqref{eq:xi}--\eqref{icl} with respect to }(h,k).

In order to show Fréchet-differentiability, then, it is enough to show that there exists a constant C>0C>0, depending only on the parameters of the system and possibly on Λ\Lambda, and an exponent s>2s>2 such that

∥(φ,μ,σ)−(φ¯,μ¯,σ¯)−(ξ,η,ρ)∥𝕎2≤C​∥(h,k)∥L2​(QT)2s.\lVert(\varphi,\mu,\sigma)-(\overline{\varphi},\overline{\mu},\overline{\sigma})-(\xi,\eta,\rho)\rVert^{2}_{\mathbb{W}}\leq C\lVert(h,k)\rVert^{s}_{L^{2}(Q_{T})^{2}}.

To do this, we introduce the additional variables

ψ:=φ−φ¯−ξ∈H1​(0,T,V∗)∩𝒞0​([0,T],H)∩L2​(0,T,V),\displaystyle\psi:=\varphi-\overline{\varphi}-\xi\in H^{1}(0,T;V^{*})\cap\mathcal{C}^{0}([0,T];H)\cap L^{2}(0,T;V),
ζ:=μ−μ¯−η∈L∞​(0,T,H)∩L2​(0,T,V),\displaystyle\zeta:=\mu-\overline{\mu}-\eta\in L^{\infty}(0,T;H)\cap L^{2}(0,T;V),

which by Theorems 4.8 and 5.3 enjoy the regularities shown above. Then, this is equivalent to showing that

where:

Fh\displaystyle F^{h} =F′​(φ)−F′​(φ¯)−F′′​(φ¯)​ξ,\displaystyle=F^{\prime}(\varphi)-F^{\prime}(\overline{\varphi})-F^{\prime\prime}(\overline{\varphi})\xi,

Note that, to be precise, system (5.13)–(5.17) has to be understood in weak sense, i.e. through a variational formulation, since only weak regularity is available for the linearised variables (ξ,η,ρ)(\xi,\eta,\rho). Before going on, we can rewrite in a better way the terms FhF^{h} and QhQ^{h}, by using the following version of Taylor’s theorem with integral remainder for any real function f∈𝒞2f\in\mathcal{C}^{2} at a point x0∈ℝx_{0}\in\mathbb{R}:

5.3 Adjoint system and optimality conditions

In order to write down the necessary conditions of optimality in a form which is suitable for applications, we now introduce the adjoint system to the optimal control problem (CP). Indeed, we fix an optimal state (φ¯,μ¯,σ¯)=𝒮⁡(u¯,v¯)(\overline{\varphi},\overline{\mu},\overline{\sigma})=\mathcal{S}(\overline{u},\overline{v}). Then, by using the formal Lagrangian method with adjoint variables (p,q,r)(p,q,r), one can find that the adjoint system, which is formally solved by these variables, has the following form:

−∂tp+AF′′(φ¯)q+Baq−BJ∗q−P′(φ¯)(σ¯−μ¯)(p−r)\displaystyle-\partial_{t}p+AF^{\prime\prime}(\overline{\varphi})q+Baq-BJ\ast q-P^{\prime}(\overline{\varphi})(\overline{\sigma}-\overline{\mu})(p-r)
+p​𝕙′​(φ¯)​u¯=αQ​(φ¯−φQ)\displaystyle\hskip 20.00003pt+p\mathbbm{h}^{\prime}(\overline{\varphi})\overline{u}=\alpha_{Q}(\overline{\varphi}-\varphi_{Q})\hskip 20.00003pt in ​QT,\displaystyle\text{in }Q_{T}, (5.23)
−q−Δ​p+P⁡(φ¯)​(p−r)=0\displaystyle-q-\Delta p+P(\overline{\varphi})(p-r)=0\hskip 20.00003pt in ​QT,\displaystyle\text{in }Q_{T}, (5.24)
−∂tr−Δr−P(φ¯)(p−r)=βQ(σ¯−σQ)\displaystyle-\partial_{t}r-\Delta r-P(\overline{\varphi})(p-r)=\beta_{Q}(\overline{\sigma}-\sigma_{Q})\hskip 20.00003pt in ​QT,\displaystyle\text{in }Q_{T}, (5.25)

together with the following boundary and final conditions:

∂𝒏p=∂𝒏r=0\displaystyle\partial_{\boldsymbol{n}}p=\partial_{\boldsymbol{n}}r=0\hskip 20.00003pt on ​ΣT,\displaystyle\text{on }\Sigma_{T}, (5.26)
p⁡(T)=αΩ​(φ¯​(T)−φΩ),r⁡(T)=βΩ​(σ¯​(T)−σΩ)\displaystyle p(T)=\alpha_{\Omega}(\overline{\varphi}(T)-\varphi_{\Omega}),\hskip 10.00002ptr(T)=\beta_{\Omega}(\overline{\sigma}(T)-\sigma_{\Omega})\hskip 20.00003pt in ​Ω.\displaystyle\text{in }\Omega. (5.27)

First, we prove the well-posedness of this adjoint system in the following theorem.

Theorem 5.7.

Assume hypotheses A1–A7, B1–B2 and C1–C5. Let (φ¯,μ¯,σ¯)∈𝕏(\overline{\varphi},\overline{\mu},\overline{\sigma})\in\mathbb{X} be the strong solution to (1.7)–(1.11), corresponding to (u¯,v¯)∈𝒰ad×𝒱ad(\overline{u},\overline{v})\in\mathcal{U}_{\text{ad}}\times\mathcal{V}_{\text{ad}}. Then, the adjoint system (5.23)–(5.27) admits a unique weak solution such that

p∈H1​(0,T,V∗)∩L∞​(0,T,H)∩L2​(0,T,V),\displaystyle p\in H^{1}(0,T;V^{*})\cap L^{\infty}(0,T;H)\cap L^{2}(0,T;V),
q∈L2​(0,T,V∗),\displaystyle q\in L^{2}(0,T;V^{*}),
r∈H1​(0,T,V∗)∩L∞​(0,T,H)∩L2​(0,T,V),\displaystyle r\in H^{1}(0,T;V^{*})\cap L^{\infty}(0,T;H)\cap L^{2}(0,T;V),

which fulfils (5.23)–(5.27) in variational formulation, i.e. it satisfies

⟨−∂tp,w⟩V+⟨q,(AF′′(φ¯)+Ba)w⟩V−B⟨q,J∗w⟩V−(P′(φ¯)(σ¯−μ¯)(p−r),w)H\displaystyle\langle-\partial_{t}p,w\rangle_{V}+\langle q,(AF^{\prime\prime}(\overline{\varphi})+Ba)w\rangle_{V}-B\langle q,J\ast w\rangle_{V}-(P^{\prime}(\overline{\varphi})(\overline{\sigma}-\overline{\mu})(p-r),w)_{H}
+(p​𝕙′​(φ¯)​u¯,w)H=(αQ​(φ¯−φQ),w)H\displaystyle\hskip 20.00003pt+(p\mathbbm{h}^{\prime}(\overline{\varphi})\overline{u},w)_{H}=(\alpha_{Q}(\overline{\varphi}-\varphi_{Q}),w)_{H} (5.28)
⟨q,w⟩V=(∇p,∇w)H+(P⁡(φ¯)​(p−r),w)H\displaystyle\langle q,w\rangle_{V}=(\nabla p,\nabla w)_{H}+(P(\overline{\varphi})(p-r),w)_{H} (5.29)
⟨−∂tr,w⟩V+(∇r,∇w)H−(P(φ¯)(p−r),w)H=(βQ(σ¯−σQ),w)H\displaystyle\langle-\partial_{t}r,w\rangle_{V}+(\nabla r,\nabla w)_{H}-(P(\overline{\varphi})(p-r),w)_{H}=(\beta_{Q}(\overline{\sigma}-\sigma_{Q}),w)_{H} (5.30)

for a.e. t∈(0,T)t\in(0,T) and for any w∈Vw\in V.

Remark 5.8.

When writing the variational formulation (5.28), we used hypothesis A2 on the symmetry of the kernel JJ to move the convolution operator onto the test function. Indeed, by a simple change of variables, one can formally see that

∫Ω(J∗q)​w​𝑑x\displaystyle\int_{\Omega}(J\ast q)\,w\,\mathrm{d}x =∫Ω(∫ΩJ⁡(x−y)​q​(y)​𝑑y)​w​(x)​𝑑x\displaystyle=\int_{\Omega}\left(\int_{\Omega}J(x-y)q(y)\,\mathrm{d}y\right)w(x)\,\mathrm{d}x
=∫Ω(∫ΩJ⁡(y−x)​w​(x)​𝑑x)​q​(y)​𝑑y=∫Ωq⁡(J∗w)​𝑑x.\displaystyle=\int_{\Omega}\left(\int_{\Omega}J(y-x)w(x)\,\mathrm{d}x\right)q(y)\,\mathrm{d}y=\int_{\Omega}q\,(J\ast w)\,\mathrm{d}x.
Proof.

We observe that (5.23)–(5.27) is a backward linear parabolic system, therefore it is not difficult to prove the existence of a solution through a Faedo-Galerkin discretisation scheme. Here we proceed with formal a priori estimates for the sake of brevity. Indeed, for the main estimate, we test (5.28) with pp, (5.30) with rr and we sum them up to obtain:

=(∇p,(AF′′(φ¯)+Ba)∇p)H+(∇p,(AF′′′(φ¯)∇φ¯+B∇a)p)H+(P(φ¯)(p−r),p)\displaystyle\hskip 10.00002pt=(\nabla p,(AF^{\prime\prime}(\overline{\varphi})+Ba)\nabla p)_{H}+(\nabla p,(AF^{\prime\prime\prime}(\overline{\varphi})\nabla\overline{\varphi}+B\nabla a)p)_{H}+(P(\overline{\varphi})(p-r),p)

≥c0​∥∇p∥H2−C​∥∇p∥H​∥∇φ¯∥L6​(Ω)​∥p∥L3​(Ω)−2​B​b∗​∥∇p∥H​∥p∥H−C⁡(∥p∥H+∥r∥H)​∥p∥H\displaystyle\hskip 10.00002pt\geq c_{0}\lVert\nabla p\rVert^{2}_{H}-C\lVert\nabla p\rVert_{H}\lVert\nabla\overline{\varphi}\rVert_{L^{6}(\Omega)}\lVert p\rVert_{L^{3}(\Omega)}-2Bb^{\ast}\lVert\nabla p\rVert_{H}\lVert p\rVert_{H}-C(\lVert p\rVert_{H}+\lVert r\rVert_{H})\lVert p\rVert_{H}

Therefore, by using Gronwall’s lemma, together with hypothesis C2, we conclude that

Moreover, by comparison in (5.28), (5.29) and (5.30), we also easily see that (5.32) implies the following estimate:

∥p∥H1​(0,T,V∗)2+∥q∥L2​(0,T,V∗)2+∥r∥H1​(0,T,V∗)2≤C⁡(∥αΩ​(φ¯​(T)−φΩ)∥H2+∥βΩ​(σ¯​(T)−σΩ)∥H2CLOSE+∫0T∥αQ(φ¯−φQ)∥2Hds+∫0T∥βQ(σ¯−σQ)∥2Hds).\begin{split}&\lVert p\rVert^{2}_{H^{1}(0,T;V^{*})}+\lVert q\rVert^{2}_{L^{2}(0,T;V^{*})}+\lVert r\rVert^{2}_{H^{1}(0,T;V^{*})}\\ &\quad\leq C\Big(\lVert\alpha_{\Omega}(\overline{\varphi}(T)-\varphi_{\Omega})\rVert^{2}_{H}+\lVert\beta_{\Omega}(\overline{\sigma}(T)-\sigma_{\Omega})\rVert^{2}_{H}\\ &\qquad\qquad+\int_{0}^{T}\lVert\alpha_{Q}(\overline{\varphi}-\varphi_{Q})\rVert^{2}_{H}\,\mathrm{d}s+\int_{0}^{T}\lVert\beta_{Q}(\overline{\sigma}-\sigma_{Q})\rVert^{2}_{H}\,\mathrm{d}s\Big).\end{split} (5.33)

All these estimates can, then, be repeated in a proper discretisation framework and, by passing to the limit, one can prove the existence of a solution with the sought regularities. Moreover, being the system linear, estimates (5.32) and (5.33) also imply the uniqueness of the solution. This concludes the proof of Theorem 5.7. ∎

To conclude, with the adjoint variables, we can finally determine and then simplify the first-order necessary conditions. Indeed, we have the following result:

Theorem 5.9.

Assume hypotheses A1–A5, B1–B2 and C1–C5. Let (u¯,v¯)∈𝒰ad×𝒱ad(\overline{u},\overline{v})\in\mathcal{U}_{\text{ad}}\times\mathcal{V}_{\text{ad}} be an optimal control for (CP) and let (φ¯,μ¯,σ¯)=𝒮⁡(u¯,v¯)∈𝕏(\overline{\varphi},\overline{\mu},\overline{\sigma})=\mathcal{S}(\overline{u},\overline{v})\in\mathbb{X} be the corresponding optimal state, i.e. the solution of (1.7)–(1.11) with such (u¯,v¯)(\overline{u},\overline{v}). Let also (p,q,r)(p,q,r) be the adjoint variables to (φ¯,σ¯,μ¯)(\overline{\varphi},\overline{\sigma},\overline{\mu}), i.e. the solutions to the adjoint system (5.23)–(5.27). Then, they satisfy the following variational inequality, which holds for any (u,v)∈𝒰ad×𝒱ad(u,v)\in\mathcal{U}_{\text{ad}}\times\mathcal{V}_{\text{ad}}:

∫0T∫Ω(−𝕙⁡(φ¯)​p+αu​u¯)​(u−u¯)​𝑑x​𝑑t+∫0T∫Ω(r+βv​v¯)​(v−v¯)​𝑑x​𝑑t≥0.\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}(-\mathbbm{h}(\overline{\varphi})p+\alpha_{u}\overline{u})(u-\overline{u})\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t+\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}(r+\beta_{v}\overline{v})(v-\overline{v})\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t\geq 0. (5.34)
Proof.

First observe that the cost functional 𝒥\mathcal{J} is convex and Fréchet-differentiable in the space 𝒞0​([0,T],H)×𝒞0​([0,T],H)×L2​(QT)×L2​(QT)\mathcal{C}^{0}([0,T];H)\times\mathcal{C}^{0}([0,T];H)\times L^{2}(Q_{T})\times L^{2}(Q_{T}). Next, in Theorem 5.5 we showed that the solution operator 𝒮\mathcal{S} is Fréchet-differentiable from 𝒰R×𝒱R⊆L∞​(QT)2\mathcal{U}_{R}\times\mathcal{V}_{R}\subseteq L^{\infty}(Q_{T})^{2} to 𝕎\mathbb{W}. Consequently, since by standard results L2​(0,T,V)∩H1​(0,T,V∗)L^{2}(0,T;V)\cap H^{1}(0,T;V^{*}) is embedded with continuity in 𝒞0​([0,T],H)\mathcal{C}^{0}([0,T];H), we also have that the operator (𝒮1,𝒮3)(\mathcal{S}_{1},\mathcal{S}_{3}) that selects the first and third components of 𝒮\mathcal{S} is Fréchet-differentiable from 𝒰R×𝒱R\mathcal{U}_{R}\times\mathcal{V}_{R} to (𝒞0​([0,T],H))2(\mathcal{C}^{0}([0,T];H))^{2}. Therefore, we can consider the reduced cost functional f:L∞​(QT)2→ℝf:L^{\infty}(Q_{T})^{2}\to\mathbb{R}, defined as

f⁡(u,v):=𝒥⁡(𝒮1​(u,v),𝒮3​(u,v),u,v),f(u,v):=\mathcal{J}(\mathcal{S}_{1}(u,v),\mathcal{S}_{3}(u,v),u,v),

which, by the chain rule, is Fréchet-differentiable in 𝒰R×𝒱R\mathcal{U}_{R}\times\mathcal{V}_{R}.

At this point, we can rewrite our optimal control problem (CP) through the reduced cost functional as the minimisation problem

arg​min(u,v)∈𝒰ad×𝒱ad⁡f​(u,v).\argmin_{(u,v)\in\,\mathcal{U}_{\text{ad}}\times\mathcal{V}_{\text{ad}}}f(u,v).

Then, if (u¯,v¯)(\overline{u},\overline{v}) is optimal, since 𝒰ad×𝒱ad\mathcal{U}_{\text{ad}}\times\mathcal{V}_{\text{ad}} is convex and ff is Fréchet-differentiable, it has to satisfy the necessary optimality condition

f′​(u¯,v¯)​[(u−u¯,v−v¯)]≥0for any ​(u,v)∈𝒰ad×𝒱ad.f^{\prime}(\overline{u},\overline{v})[(u-\overline{u},v-\overline{v})]\geq 0\hskip 10.00002pt\text{for any }(u,v)\in\mathcal{U}_{\text{ad}}\times\mathcal{V}_{\text{ad}}.

Hence, by computing explicitly the derivative of ff, we get that for any (u,v)∈𝒰ad×𝒱ad(u,v)\in\mathcal{U}_{\text{ad}}\times\mathcal{V}_{\text{ad}}

∫ΩαΩ​(φ¯​(T)−φΩ)​ξ​(T)​𝑑x+∫0T∫ΩαQ​(φ¯−φQ)​ξ​𝑑x​𝑑t\displaystyle\int_{\Omega}\alpha_{\Omega}(\overline{\varphi}(T)-\varphi_{\Omega})\xi(T)\,\mathrm{d}x+\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}\alpha_{Q}(\overline{\varphi}-\varphi_{Q})\xi\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t
+∫ΩβΩ(σ¯(T)−σΩ)ρ(T)dx+∫0T∫ΩβQ(σ¯−σQ)ρdxdt\displaystyle+\int_{\Omega}\beta_{\Omega}(\overline{\sigma}(T)-\sigma_{\Omega})\rho(T)\,\mathrm{d}x+\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}\beta_{Q}(\overline{\sigma}-\sigma_{Q})\rho\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t
+∫0T∫Ωαuu¯(u−u¯)dxdt+∫0T∫Ωβvv¯(v−v¯)dxdt≥0,\displaystyle+\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}\alpha_{u}\overline{u}(u-\overline{u})\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t+\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}\beta_{v}\overline{v}(v-\overline{v})\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t\geq 0,

where ξ=D​𝒮1​(u¯,v¯)​[u−u¯,v−v¯]\xi=D\mathcal{S}_{1}(\overline{u},\overline{v})[u-\overline{u},v-\overline{v}] and ρ=D​𝒮3​(u¯,v¯)​[u−u¯,v−v¯]\rho=D\mathcal{S}_{3}(\overline{u},\overline{v})[u-\overline{u},v-\overline{v}] are the components of the solution (ξ,η,ρ)(\xi,\eta,\rho) to the linearised system (5.2)–(5.6) in (φ¯,μ¯,σ¯)(\overline{\varphi},\overline{\mu},\overline{\sigma}) corresponding to h=u−u¯h=u-\overline{u} and k=v−v¯k=v-\overline{v}. Note that in what follows we are going to write all the integral terms as if they were in strong form, however keep in mind that, in our regularity setting, all products involving time-derivatives, laplacians and qq have to be intended as duality products.

Now observe that the right-hand sides and the final conditions of the adjoint system appear in this inequality, therefore by substituting equations (5.23), (5.25) and (5.27) in the previous expression, we find that for any (u,v)∈𝒰ad×𝒱ad(u,v)\in\mathcal{U}_{\text{ad}}\times\mathcal{V}_{\text{ad}}

∫Ωp(T)ξ(T)dx+∫0T∫Ω(−∂tp+AF′′(φ¯)q+Baq−BJ∗q\displaystyle\int_{\Omega}p(T)\xi(T)\,\mathrm{d}x+\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}\Big(-\partial_{t}p+AF^{\prime\prime}(\overline{\varphi})q+Baq-BJ\ast q
OPEN−P′​(φ¯)​(σ¯−μ¯)​(p−r)+p​𝕙′​(φ¯)​u¯)​ξ​𝑑x​𝑑t+∫Ωr⁡(T)​ρ​(T)​𝑑x\displaystyle\hskip 20.00003pt-P^{\prime}(\overline{\varphi})(\overline{\sigma}-\overline{\mu})(p-r)+p\mathbbm{h}^{\prime}(\overline{\varphi})\overline{u}\Big)\xi\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t+\int_{\Omega}r(T)\rho(T)\,\mathrm{d}x
+∫0T∫Ω(−∂tr−Δr−P(φ¯)(p−r))ρdxdt\displaystyle\hskip 10.00002pt+\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}\big(-\partial_{t}r-\Delta r-P(\overline{\varphi})(p-r)\big)\rho\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t
+∫0T∫Ωαuu¯(u−u¯)dxdt+∫0T∫Ωβvv¯(v−v¯)dxdt≥0.\displaystyle\hskip 10.00002pt+\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}\alpha_{u}\overline{u}(u-\overline{u})\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t+\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}\beta_{v}\overline{v}(v-\overline{v})\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t\geq 0.

Now we integrate by parts in time, by using also the initial conditions (5.6) on the linearised system, and in space, by using the boundary conditions (5.26) and (5.5), and, after cancellations, we find that equivalently for any (u,v)∈𝒰ad×𝒱ad(u,v)\in\mathcal{U}_{\text{ad}}\times\mathcal{V}_{\text{ad}}

∫0T∫Ω(p​ξt+A​F′′​(φ¯)​ξ​q+B​a​ξ​q−B⁡(J∗ξ)​q−P′​(φ¯)​(σ¯−μ¯)​(p−r)​ξ+p​𝕙′​(φ¯)​u¯​ξ)​𝑑x​𝑑t\displaystyle\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}\Big(p\xi_{t}+AF^{\prime\prime}(\overline{\varphi})\xi q+Ba\xi q-B(J\ast\xi)q-P^{\prime}(\overline{\varphi})(\overline{\sigma}-\overline{\mu})(p-r)\xi+p\mathbbm{h}^{\prime}(\overline{\varphi})\overline{u}\,\xi\Big)\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t
+∫0T∫Ω(ρtr−Δρr−P(φ¯)(p−r)ρ)dxdt\displaystyle\hskip 10.00002pt+\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}\big(\rho_{t}r-\Delta\rho\,r-P(\overline{\varphi})(p-r)\rho\big)\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t
+∫0T∫Ωαuu¯(u−u¯)dxdt+∫0T∫Ωβvv¯(v−v¯)dxdt≥0,\displaystyle\hskip 10.00002pt+\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}\alpha_{u}\overline{u}(u-\overline{u})\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t+\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}\beta_{v}\overline{v}(v-\overline{v})\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t\geq 0,

where we also used the symmetry of the kernel JJ. By factoring out pp, qq and rr respectively, we can rewrite the previous inequality as

∫0T∫Ωp⁡(ξt−P⁡(φ¯)​ρ−P′​(φ¯)​(σ¯−μ¯)​ξ+𝕙′​(φ¯)​u¯​ξ)​𝑑x​𝑑t\displaystyle\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}p\left(\xi_{t}-P(\overline{\varphi})\rho-P^{\prime}(\overline{\varphi})(\overline{\sigma}-\overline{\mu})\xi+\mathbbm{h}^{\prime}(\overline{\varphi})\overline{u}\,\xi\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t
+∫0T∫Ωq(AF′′(φ¯)ξ+Baξ−BJ∗ξ)dxdt\displaystyle\hskip 10.00002pt+\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}q\left(AF^{\prime\prime}(\overline{\varphi})\xi+Ba\xi-BJ\ast\xi\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t
+∫0T∫Ωr(ρt−Δρ+P(φ¯)ρ+P′(φ¯)(σ¯−μ¯)ξ)dxdt\displaystyle\hskip 10.00002pt+\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}r\left(\rho_{t}-\Delta\rho+P(\overline{\varphi})\rho+P^{\prime}(\overline{\varphi})(\overline{\sigma}-\overline{\mu})\xi\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t
+∫0T∫Ωαuu¯(u−u¯)dxdt+∫0T∫Ωβvv¯(v−v¯)dxdt≥0.\displaystyle\hskip 10.00002pt+\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}\alpha_{u}\overline{u}(u-\overline{u})\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t+\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}\beta_{v}\overline{v}(v-\overline{v})\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t\geq 0.

Finally, we use equation (5.24) and again integration by parts to also get that

0\displaystyle 0 =∫0T∫Ω(−q−Δp+P(φ¯)(p−r))ηdxdt=∫0T∫Ω−ηq−Δηp+P(φ¯)(p−r)ηdxdt.\displaystyle=\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}\left(-q-\Delta p+P(\overline{\varphi})(p-r)\right)\eta\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t=\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}-\eta q-\Delta\eta\,p+P(\overline{\varphi})(p-r)\eta\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t.

Then, by adding this to the previous inequality, we at last infer that for any (u,v)∈𝒰ad×𝒱ad(u,v)\in\mathcal{U}_{\text{ad}}\times\mathcal{V}_{\text{ad}}

∫0T∫Ωp⁡(ξt−Δ​η−P⁡(φ¯)​(ρ−η)−P′​(φ¯)​(σ¯−μ¯)​ξ+𝕙′​(φ¯)​u¯​ξ)​𝑑x​𝑑t\displaystyle\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}p\left(\xi_{t}-\Delta\eta-P(\overline{\varphi})(\rho-\eta)-P^{\prime}(\overline{\varphi})(\overline{\sigma}-\overline{\mu})\xi+\mathbbm{h}^{\prime}(\overline{\varphi})\overline{u}\,\xi\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t
+∫0T∫Ωq(−η+AF′′(φ¯)ξ+Baξ−BJ∗ξ)dxdt\displaystyle\hskip 10.00002pt+\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}q\left(-\eta+AF^{\prime\prime}(\overline{\varphi})\xi+Ba\xi-BJ\ast\xi\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t
+∫0T∫Ωr(ρt−Δρ+P(φ¯)(ρ−η)+P′(φ¯)(σ¯−μ¯)ξ)dxdt\displaystyle\hskip 10.00002pt+\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}r\left(\rho_{t}-\Delta\rho+P(\overline{\varphi})(\rho-\eta)+P^{\prime}(\overline{\varphi})(\overline{\sigma}-\overline{\mu})\xi\right)\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t
+∫0T∫Ωαuu¯(u−u¯)dxdt+∫0T∫Ωβvv¯(v−v¯)dxdt≥0.\displaystyle\hskip 10.00002pt+\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}\alpha_{u}\overline{u}(u-\overline{u})\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t+\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}\beta_{v}\overline{v}(v-\overline{v})\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t\geq 0.

To conclude, we notice that the expressions enclosed in the parentheses are exactly the equations (5.2), (5.3), (5.4) of the linearised system, up to their source terms. Hence, by substituting those into our inequality, we find that for any (u,v)∈𝒰ad×𝒱ad(u,v)\in\mathcal{U}_{\text{ad}}\times\mathcal{V}_{\text{ad}}

∫0T∫Ω−p𝕙(φ¯)(u−u¯)dxdt+∫0T∫Ωr(v−v¯)dxdt\displaystyle\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}-p\,\mathbbm{h}(\overline{\varphi})(u-\overline{u})\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t+\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}r(v-\overline{v})\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t
+∫0T∫Ωαuu¯(u−u¯)dxdt+∫0T∫Ωβvv¯(v−v¯)dxdt≥0,\displaystyle\hskip 10.00002pt+\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}\alpha_{u}\overline{u}(u-\overline{u})\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t+\int_{0}^{T}\int_{\Omega}\beta_{v}\overline{v}(v-\overline{v})\,\mathrm{d}x\,\mathrm{d}t\geq 0,

which is exactly (5.34). This concludes the proof of Theorem 5.9. ∎

Remark 5.10.

Observe that, since 𝒰ad×𝒱ad\mathcal{U}_{\text{ad}}\times\mathcal{V}_{\text{ad}} is closed and convex, (5.34) means that, if αu>0\alpha_{u}>0 and βv>0\beta_{v}>0, the optimal control (u¯,v¯)(\overline{u},\overline{v}) is exactly the L2​(QT)2L^{2}(Q_{T})^{2}-orthogonal projection of (αu−1​𝕙​(φ¯)​p,−βv−1​r)(\alpha_{u}^{-1}\mathbbm{h}(\overline{\varphi})\,p,-\beta_{v}^{-1}r) onto 𝒰ad×𝒱ad\mathcal{U}_{\text{ad}}\times\mathcal{V}_{\text{ad}}. In particular, it can be shown that, due to the structure of 𝒰ad×𝒱ad\mathcal{U}_{\text{ad}}\times\mathcal{V}_{\text{ad}}, the above L2​(QT)2L^{2}(Q_{T})^{2}-projection has the explicit form:

u¯​(x,t)=min⁡{umax​(x,t),max⁡{αu−1​𝕙​(φ¯)​p​(x,t),umin​(x,t)}}for a.e. ​(x,t)∈QT,\displaystyle\overline{u}(x,t)=\min\left\{u_{\text{max}}(x,t),\max\left\{\alpha_{u}^{-1}\mathbbm{h}(\overline{\varphi})\,p(x,t),u_{\text{min}}(x,t)\right\}\right\}\hskip 10.00002pt\text{for a.e. }(x,t)\in Q_{T},
v¯​(x,t)=min⁡{vmax​(x,t),max⁡{−βv−1​r​(x,t),vmin​(x,t)}}for a.e. ​(x,t)∈QT.\displaystyle\overline{v}(x,t)=\min\left\{v_{\text{max}}(x,t),\max\left\{-\beta_{v}^{-1}r(x,t),v_{\text{min}}(x,t)\right\}\right\}\hskip 10.00002pt\text{for a.e. }(x,t)\in Q_{T}.

To get this kind of explicit form, it is crucial for 𝒰ad\mathcal{U}_{\text{ad}} and 𝒱ad\mathcal{V}_{\text{ad}} to be described by box constraints in L∞​(QT)L^{\infty}(Q_{T}). We stress that our new maximal regularity strategy allowed us to get highly regular solutions by only assuming such constraints on the controls. In this sense, the result presented here can be thought as a partial improvement to the optimality conditions proved in [17], where we also needed the additional H1​(0,T,H)H^{1}(0,T;H)-regularity on the control uu.
